title: Payments made at the request of State officials to organizations the City also pays
question: Which State officials asked donors to pay organizations that San Francisco funds, who paid, and how much?
finding: State officials reported $62.7 million in payments made at their request, since 2015, to 21 organizations the City also pays. $61.9 million of it is in 11 rows filed by Gavin Newsom, the largest $45.6 million to Enterprise Community Partners Inc. ("To support Project Homekey."). The pattern that stands out is local: Matt Haney (Assembly) reported 50 payments totalling $387,602 to Center For New Music San Francisco Inc between 2023 and 2026, from 35 payors including Amazon.com Services LLC $50,000; Northern California Carpenters Regional Council $45,000; Uber Technologies Inc. $25,000; CA Apartment Association $25,000, most often filed under the purpose "Legislative" and described as "Donation to Center for New Music San Francisco 501 (c)(3) -- Joy to the City Event". The City paid that organization $3.2 million in fiscal 2019 to 2026, and it carries this sign here: Federal tax exemption shown as revoked 2022-02-15, not reinstated.
how: Read the 2,797 payments of 2015 to 2026 in the Fair Political Practices Commission's file of behested-payment reports (Form 803) that touch San Francisco or its officials. Kept those whose recipient is, by name, a non-government organization the City paid $100,000 or more in fiscal 2019 to 2026, and added them by official and recipient. An official's name is grouped across the spellings in the file. Payors that look like private individuals are counted but not named. The column for City payees among the payors uses the same $1 million cut as this project's earlier interests screen, which listed those payments one by one; this table adds every other payor and groups by official.
limits: This file is the officials' own reports of doing so. The published file has no field saying whether a payor had business before the official, so that cannot be shown from it: the record that would supply it is the payor's own lobbying reports to the Secretary of State, which are not on disk for these payors. "Legislative" is one of the three purpose labels that appear in the file (with "Charitable" and "Governmental"); the file does not define them. The recipient named on a report may be holding the money for an event or a project it hosts. Payors are grouped on a tidied name, so one company filed under two different names counts twice. Recipients are matched to City payees by name.
